title: fix(app-shell): teach the drill URL dialect to spell `is_not_null`
body:
Fixes #9508

The drill `filter[...]` URL dialect can now spell IS NOT NULL, so the three producer
spellings that used to vanish on the escape hatch reach the destination list.

Placeholders below are written as UPPERCASE WORDS rather than in angle brackets, because
this platform silently eats tag-shaped fragments from a stored body — including inside
backticks and fenced blocks.

## The card's table, re-derived rather than inherited

Corpus: this branch's base `aced50d2e` (`origin/main` at the time — the dispatch named the
same commit, and it was still the tip when re-read), measured 2026-09-18T21:15:12Z by
running the tree's own `convertFiltersToAST` and `serializeDrillFilterParams` in one
command, with two controls lit in the same run. LINES, not counts:

```text
spelling={ $null: true }              | convertFiltersToAST=["f","is_null",true]     | url=filter[f][null]=true  | readBack=[["f","is_null",true]]
spelling={ $exists: false }           | convertFiltersToAST=["f","is_null",true]     | url=(dropped - superset)  | readBack=[]
spelling={ $null: false }             | convertFiltersToAST=["f","is_not_null",true] | url=(dropped - superset)  | readBack=[]
spelling={ $exists: true }            | convertFiltersToAST=["f","is_not_null",true] | url=(dropped - superset)  | readBack=[]
CONTROL equality { f: "v" }           | convertFiltersToAST=["f","=","v"]            | url=filter[f]=v           | readBack=[["f","=","v"]]
CONTROL range { $gte: 5 }             | convertFiltersToAST=["f",">=",5]             | url=filter[f][gte]=5      | readBack=[["f",">=","5"]]
```

The card's table reproduces exactly. The two controls are what make the three `(dropped)`
rows a reading rather than a broken probe.

After the change, on `9c471932d`, the same command prints `filter[f][null]=true` for the
first two rows and `filter[f][null]=false` for the other two, with both controls unmoved.

## The card's own non-urgency measurement, re-taken

It still holds. `buildDatasetDrillFilter` emits `{ $null: true }` for every empty-bucket
shape the wire carries (empty string, a SQL NULL arriving as `null`, an absent key) and
nothing else; its two other outputs are a plain equality value and a `{ $gte, $lt }` date
range, both lit as controls in the same run. No machine producer on that path reaches the
new spellings.

So this is a **latent-surface repair, not a live regression**, and the PR claims nothing
more. The claim is now pinned in `drillNotNullDialect-9508.test.tsx` so it reddens if a
producer ever starts emitting one of the three, instead of being restated in prose.

## What is WRONG in the card, measured

The card says the reachable route is "an authored widget filter composed into the drill
(`composeDrillFilter`)". That route cannot in fact deliver two of the three spellings.
`composeDrillFilter` lowers through the spec's `parseFilterAST`, which canonicalises
`is_not_null` back to `{ $null: false }` — so an authored `$exists` is already gone before
the serializer sees it:

```text
composeDrillFilter widget={amount:{"$exists":true}}   => {"$and":[{"amount":{"$null":false}},{"stage":"won"}]}
composeDrillFilter widget={amount:{"$exists":false}}  => {"$and":[{"amount":{"$null":true}},{"stage":"won"}]}
composeDrillFilter widget={amount:"CONTROL-value"}    => {"$and":[{"amount":"CONTROL-value"},{"stage":"won"}]}
```

⇒ through composition, `{ $exists: false }` was **already spellable** and only
`{ $null: false }` was lost. The route that delivers `$exists` verbatim is the
**uncomposed** one: `ObjectMetricWidget` hands `DrillDownDrawer` its own resolved filter,
which reaches `openRecordList` through no canonicaliser at all. That is why the write side
reads BOTH producer keys — reading only the canonical one would have closed the composed
route and left the uncomposed one degrading exactly as before, for an author who picks
"is not empty" in the dataset filter inspector (which writes the `$exists` pair). Both
routes are driven end to end in the new test.

## The repair

`filter[FIELD][null]` now carries a DIRECTION rather than a flag.

- **write** — one resolver answers "which way does this operator object ask about
  emptiness": `$null` verbatim, `$exists` inverted, a non-boolean under either key is not
  a direction and still writes nothing. `$null` wins deterministically when both are
  present and disagree, which is a superset whichever way it goes (such an object asks for
  `is_null` AND `is_not_null`, selecting no rows at all).
- **read** — `=true` stays `is_null` byte-for-byte; `=false` becomes `is_not_null`. Every
  other value is still dropped like an unknown suffix, never downgraded.
- **chip** — its own arm, handing out the filter builder's existing `isNotNull` operator
  key. All ten locale packs already define it and it is already in the denominator of
  `filter-builder-operator-locale-parity.test.ts`, so no eleventh string is authored.
- **delete / save-as-view** — both already cover it: the delete is prefix-based, and
  `is_not_null` is a canonical `ViewFilterRule` word that reaches `normalizeFilterOperator`
  unbridged. Probed against the installed spec with a lit negative control
  (`BOGUS_CONTROL` normalizes to itself and `safeParse` is `false`), and pinned.

⚠️ objectui#9159 ruled `[null]=false` deliberately NOT an operator, on a premise it stated
outright: the dialect could not WRITE one, so a read-side operator would have had no
producer. This change supplies that producer in the same commit, so the premise is
**discharged rather than overridden**. The pins that recorded the refusal were updated in
place, not deleted, and the two exhaustive `NULL_FILTER` object pins were narrowed to
assert the five members whose MOVEMENT would falsify their file's claim — an exhaustive
`toEqual` there reddens on any future spelling without any of those five having moved.

## The published surface does not move

- Round trip pinned in both directions for all four spellings, against the expectation
  **computed by `convertFiltersToAST`** rather than transcribed from it.
- A mixed drill's exact query string is pinned, so a bookmarked URL keeps its bytes:
  `filter[stage]=won&filter[owner][null]=true&filter[close_date][gte]=...&filter[close_date][lt]=...`
- `URL_FILTER_OPS` and `RANGE_OP_PARAM` are untouched — no range operator was added, and
  putting this pair in the range map would send it through `ObjectDataPage`'s alias bridge
  and lose the condition from a saved view.
- The equality-only object route still executes no operator suffix (objectui#9196's
  boundary), with a lit control.

## Ablation — two legs, both proven on disk

Run through `ablation-replace.mjs`, which asserts the anchor hit, the blob change, and the
restore (blob equality against HEAD plus an empty `git diff HEAD`), with a trap on
EXIT/INT/TERM against an absolute path. Predeclared direction for both: RED.

Leg A, the WRITE arm reverted to "only `$null === true` writes":

```text
anchor "const direction = nullDirection(ops);" x1 -> x0
blob   4ff2b0017c046126f5ef3ebc67dc072dab290794 -> aa9de337675e8fdd4c5c1c2efc2ccd92439e13da
Tests  9 failed | 6 passed (15)
restore: blob == HEAD (4ff2b0017c04) and `git diff HEAD` is empty
```

Leg B, the READ arm deleted:

```text
anchor "else if (value === NULL_FILTER.notFlag) ..." x1 -> x0
blob   4ff2b0017c046126f5ef3ebc67dc072dab290794 -> e21f846c31508722eae2ffbc0266b7171f466749
Tests  7 failed | 8 passed (15)
restore: blob == HEAD (4ff2b0017c04) and `git diff HEAD` is empty
```

Both legs kill the dispatch's named input — a drill carrying `{ $exists: true }`, which the
old dialect drops and the new one carries. The tests that stay green in both legs are the
`{ $null: true }` control, the equality control, the record that composition erases
`$exists`, and the `buildDatasetDrillFilter` non-urgency pins — i.e. the ablation is
targeted, not total. `git status --porcelain` is empty after both.

## A pending changeset this change falsified, corrected in place

`check:changeset-claims` reported that this diff touches files named by the pending
objectui#9159 changeset, and asked for a read. One paragraph of it had gone false — it
declares `[null]=false` is not a second operator. It is corrected, prose only, frontmatter
untouched (`minor` at base, `minor` now), stating the boundary as that card shipped it and
pointing at this one. `check:changeset-overwrite` reports the modification as its own
documented case 2 and exits 0.

## Acceptance notes

Out-of-scope observations, noted and deliberately not filed:

- `DrillDownDrawer`'s report arm composes `{ $and: [reportFilter, filter] }` by hand
  instead of routing through `composeDrillFilter`, which is the sink objectui#8944 /
  objectui#9024 / objectui#9137 moved every other drill seam onto. Noted, not filed:
  nothing measured it misbehaving here, and the array arm that broke the others does not
  reach that line. Who would meet it: the next seat routing a report drill through the
  shared sink.
- `convertFiltersToAST` collapses `$exists` and `$null` onto the same two AST operators,
  while the dataset filter inspector offers `isEmpty` / `isNull` as distinct rows — so an
  author's choice between them is not recoverable after a round trip through the AST. That
  is upstream of this dialect and predates it. Noted, not filed. Who would meet it: a seat
  working on the inspector's read-back.

Neither is a reproducible defect, a declared-contract violation, or a metadata trap, so
neither meets the filing bar.

## Verification

- `pnpm exec vitest run` over the five affected app-shell view test files plus the new one
  — all green.
- `pnpm --filter @object-ui/app-shell run type-check` (`tsc --noEmit` AND
  `tsc -p tsconfig.test.json`, so the new test file is covered) after building the
  dependency closure — green.
- Targeted `eslint --no-inline-config` over the six touched files: 6 files linted,
  0 errors, 0 warnings, read from `--format json`. The narrowing is safe to read as a
  measurement because this repo's flat config extends `tseslint.configs.recommended` and
  declares no `parserOptions.project` / `projectService` — type-aware linting is off, so a
  diff that touches no config cannot move the verdict on any file it does not contain. The
  repo-wide `eslint .` run stays CI's.
- Gates: `check:control-bytes`, `check:new-line-citations`, `check:changeset-presence`,
  `check:changeset-claims`, `check:changeset-no-major`, `check:changeset-overwrite`,
  `check:pending-changeset-literals`, `check:test-path-roots`, `check:vi-mock-specifiers`,
  `check:i18n-keys`, `check:i18n-drift`, `check:i18n-dead-keys`,
  `check:unreferenced-sources` — all exit 0.
- `check-governed-queue-guard.mjs --test` over the diff: NOT GOVERNED.
